references.text: Moses' upbringing in Pharaoh's house, which provides context for his adulthood and his visit to his brothers.
Describes the forced labor and burdens (סִבְלֹת) of the Hebrews that Moses saw when he went out to his brothers.
The same word for burdens (סִבְלֹת) is used regarding the Israelites' slavery under the Egyptians.
God promises to free the Israelites from the Egyptians' burdens (סִבְלֹת), the same theme Moses observed.
Stephen's speech refers directly to this event where Moses visited his brothers and saw an Egyptian striking a Hebrew.
Moses chose to suffer hardship with God's people rather than enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin, a reference to his identification with the Hebrews.
Joseph was sent to check on his brothers' welfare, using similar expressions about going out to his brothers.
Narrative connection: Moses' initial identification with his brothers (2:11) and his later call to return to them (4:18).
Direct allusion: Acts 7:24 interprets and confirms the event in Exod 2:11 as part of God's plan.
Theological contrast: Solidarity with brothers (2:11) versus the demand to go against brothers for God's glory (32:29).
